## Results {#sec-results}

### Decay Prediction Accuracy

Our adaptive decay model significantly outperforms traditional spaced repetition algorithms on the FSRS-Anki test set.

![Decay Prediction Performance: Memory Palace vs State-of-the-Art](figures/decay_prediction_comparison.png){#fig-decay-comparison}

**Key Finding (RQ3)**: Memory Palace achieves **57% lower MAE** (0.094 vs 0.218) compared to both SM-2 and FSRS. This improvement stems from incorporating the SMASHIN SCOPE encoding strength as a decay modifier—memories with higher encoding scores decay more slowly, matching empirical observations from method of loci research [@dresler2017mnemonic].

### Learning Efficiency

![Learning Efficiency: Reviews Required vs Final Retention](figures/learning_efficiency.png){#fig-learning-efficiency}

Memory Palace with full SMASHIN SCOPE encoding (S=12) achieves **100% retention with only 3.7 reviews per card**, compared to SM-2's 18.6 reviews—a **5x improvement** in learning efficiency. This validates the method of loci's effectiveness documented in neuroscience literature [@mallow2015durable].

### Retrieval Performance

| Method | Recall@1 | Recall@3 | MRR | Avg Context (KB) | Latency (ms) |
|--------|----------|----------|-----|------------------|--------------|
| Flat RAG | 0.72 | 0.84 | 0.77 | 46.5 | 245 |
| HyDE | 0.75 | 0.86 | 0.79 | 52.3 | 312 |
| RAPTOR | 0.78 | 0.88 | 0.82 | 38.2 | 287 |
| GraphRAG | 0.81 | 0.91 | 0.85 | 41.7 | 356 |
| **Memory Palace** | **0.89** | **0.96** | **0.92** | **1.2** | **89** |

: Retrieval Performance Comparison {#tbl-retrieval-results}

**Key Finding (RQ1)**: Memory Palace achieves **Recall@1 of 89%** compared to GraphRAG's 81%, while using **97% less context** (1.2KB vs 46.5KB). The hierarchical index enables efficient 2-hop retrieval without loading the full corpus.

### Context Reduction

![Context Size Scaling: Flat vs Hierarchical Retrieval](figures/context_reduction.png){#fig-context-reduction}

At 1,000 memories, hierarchical retrieval reduces context from **500KB to 2.5KB**—a **99.5% reduction**. This enables Memory Palace to scale to large knowledge bases without exhausting LLM context windows.

### Hallucination Prevention

| Method | Precision | Recall | F1 | False Positive Rate |
|--------|-----------|--------|-----|---------------------|
| Standard RAG | 0.62 | 0.58 | 0.60 | 0.38 |
| Self-Consistency | 0.71 | 0.65 | 0.68 | 0.29 |
| NLI-Based | 0.74 | 0.69 | 0.71 | 0.26 |
| SelfCheckGPT | 0.78 | 0.72 | 0.75 | 0.22 |
| **MP Verify Tokens** | **0.94** | **0.91** | **0.92** | **0.06** |

: Hallucination Detection Performance {#tbl-hallucination-results}

**Key Finding (RQ2)**: Verification tokens achieve **F1 score of 0.92** for hallucination detection, significantly outperforming SelfCheckGPT (0.75) and NLI-based methods (0.71). The approach is also computationally cheaper—a simple string match vs. multiple model inferences.

### SMASHIN SCOPE Effect on Decay

![Effect of SMASHIN SCOPE Encoding on Memory Decay](figures/smashin_scope_effect.png){#fig-smashin-decay}

Memories with full SMASHIN SCOPE encoding (score=12) maintain **50% retention for 46 days** compared to **3.5 days** for unencoded memories—a **13x improvement** in durability. This aligns with neuroscience findings that multi-channel encoding creates more robust memory traces [@bower1970analysis].
